niche: Mind Hacks, AI Secrets, Bizarre Body Science & Hidden Power Dynamics

ideas.title: The Interactive Color Mind-Reading Test
ideas.angle: A live interactive challenge where the viewer follows three mental commands to arrive at a 'random' color, but the narration forces them into one specific choice. Ends with a command to 'comment if I got it right' to drive massive engagement.

hook.en: Pick any color. I'll read your mind.

ideas.reason: Interactive 'mind-reading' shorts consistently hit 100%+ APV because the viewer must wait for the reveal to see if they were 'caught'. Similar concepts like 'Think of a tool' are proven viral evergreen formats.
sources: Psychology of Numerical and Color Association (Wegner, 1987)

ideas.title: The Negative Afterimage Brain Glitch
ideas.angle: The video shows a high-contrast inverted image and forces the viewer to stare at a white dot for 15 seconds. When the screen turns blank white, they see a full-color image that isn't there. High retention due to the required 'staring' time.

hook.en: Stare at this dot. Do not blink.

ideas.reason: Forced-focus challenges (Type 1 Archetype) guarantee high VVSA because they present an immediate physical challenge. The physiological 'payoff' at the end ensures the viewer watches until the final second.
sources: Opponent Process Theory of Color Vision (Hering)

ideas.title: The Subtle Dominance Shoulder Tap
ideas.angle: Explains a specific micro-behavioral power play: how placing a hand on someone's shoulder during a handshake or greeting instantly establishes a hierarchy. Teaches viewers how to spot it and how to neutralize it to regain respect.

hook.en: You are being manipulated by this gesture.

ideas.reason: Social survival and 'Power Dynamics' (Type 3 Archetype) are high-velocity topics. Viewers are highly motivated to learn 'forbidden' social cues that give them an edge or protect them from being dominated.
sources: The Definitive Book of Body Language (Pease & Pease)
Joe Navarro's FBI Body Language Analysis
